summary: Authored women enter the island through their faction's own production, carrying a written identity where an ordinary worker carries a rolled one, so no code anywhere branches on whether a person was written or generated

coordination.notes: The character authority settled this design rather than me inventing one: 'Notables and generated ordinary women use the same population and membership rules; there is no separate protected heroine caste', and 'Ordinary women are named generated workers or fighters produced by buildings. Notables use the same person record with authored identity.' So a notable is not a caste, a placement or a spawn -- she is the person a faction's building produces when its turn comes, with a written identity substituted for a rolled one at exactly one line. She takes the definition's sprite and combat profile, so she is not stronger for being written, and the recruitment proof drives approach/talk/recruit/assign through the same verbs a generated woman uses. Scale was the point of the task: the heroine/named-person split is what makes a roster of dozens affordable, because the validator requires the seven-skill kit (four powers, an ultimate, a party passive, a strategic passive) only for kind heroine. Betty keeps her kit; Marisol, Neriah and Su-zhen are notables with authored identity, competence domains and recruitment content, promotable later by authoring kits. Adding another is one record, two placeholder entries and two manifest lines -- no code.

pass: all three suites, no ERROR line, 'Current 2D Godot verification passed'

checks.command: FIRST DESIGN WAS WRONG AND THE SUITE CAUGHT IT
checks.result: The first cut placed notables standing on the board at tick 0. Six tests failed: two fixtures I expected, and four behavioural tests I did not -- elven_wardens_replace_slowly, holding_salvage_actual_siege, home_defense_recalls_one_sieger, ordinary_production_uses_both_sexes. world.rs:9082 asserts no faction people exist at start: the island begins with Michael alone and everyone else arrives through production. Standing four grown women at faction holdings before the first tick broke that invariant. Rebuilt so a notable is produced rather than placed, which is what the authority said in the first place. Four of the six failures then resolved themselves.

scenario_rules() initialised the notable roster empty, so a legacy campaign migrated into this scenario would have quietly never raised any notable at all. Fixed by resolving the roster wherever rules are built from a definition, with from_scenario keeping the refusals. Not a test artifact -- a shipped-silently bug the migration proof caught.

checks.command: REAL TRAP FOUND BY the recruitment test on its first run
checks.result: recruit_island_person reads person.recruitment_offer for everyone, and the persona pools fill that field only for generated women, so the first placement of Betty was silently unrecruitable: walkable to, talkable to, never askable. Closed with island.recruitmentOffer/companionResponse plus a validator rule that refuses a rostered adult woman who lacks an offer.

checks.command: identity invariant checked every tick for 600 ticks
checks.result: pass: a notable is either standing or recorded dead, never both and never neither. She does die out there -- she is an ordinary deckhand in a real war -- and the ordinary death path (world.rs:3403) preserves every actor as a casualty, so the production guard's !casualties.contains_key stops her being quietly produced a second time. This is the authority's 'exactly one incarnation of each identity'.

checks.command: equality and migration proofs kept pointed at the base island
checks.result: Both fixtures predate the notables, who now legitimately share the production stream. Rather than regenerating the fixtures -- which would bake the new behaviour into the baseline and destroy its ability to catch the next accidental drift -- both proofs run the pack with placements cleared, and the notables are proved by their own two tests instead.
